ideas.title: Land yacht: the cart sails before it has a motor
ideas.critique: This is the only pitch where the player drives something fast through a force they have to read, and stalling, flapping and heeling are real feel, not a readout. The risk is the sail: if the cloth-in-solved-wind coupling turns into a fitted lift coefficient on one panel, it becomes a rig with a sail mesh on top. It also skips the electric road it claims to serve.

ideas.title: Sand fences: the drift grows live (project wind, next step)
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: The physics is honest (saltation, saturation length, repose on a re-solved flow) and there is something to build on, but the planned film is one more fixed time-lapse of a simulation left alone, which is exactly the form the last ten posts are stuck in. Riding the ramp it made is the payoff, and it needs a cart that does not exist yet.

ideas.title: The friends ride the empty cart down the slip face
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Real masses tumbling out of a slewing cart is a clip people would share, and laying planks gives the player a real choice. But one shove and then watching is close to 'release it and see', and it runs the cart downhill before the road ever pushes one.

ideas.title: A kite that pulls the generator
ideas.critique: Tying a skill (flying figure-eights in gusts) straight to a filament that pulses on each power stroke is a strong, readable loop, and it chains three existing solvers in a way the island has never done. The glowing wire repeats a recent post, and a kite whose lift is a fudge on top of VBD cloth would undercut the whole thing.

ideas.title: Sandstorm night buries the road
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is mostly burying what the island has, and the road it buries has not been laid yet, so the first session would show a buried road that never existed. Digging with Lumi's beak is the only new thing to play with, and as pitched it is thin.

ideas.title: Lumi's wings learn to carry a plank
ideas.critique: Hands that really hold things, with the load changing Lumi's gait, are a lasting body ability that every later build step uses, and the wobbling waddle is a nice thing to watch. On its own it is a carrying animation, with no goal beyond putting the plank down.

ideas.title: A windmill with sails you choose
ideas.critique: This is the generator step the road names, and choosing sail area against tearing is a fair tradeoff. But blade element momentum fed by one hub speed is a one-case rig, a windmill is an expected building, and a dusk film of it turning alone repeats the device-left-running form.

ideas.title: Dune avalanches under the friends' feet
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A slope failure that carries bodies by friction is a new way the ground moves, and the climbing puzzle is real. The payoff (the ground gives way under the friends) is the same as the old ice post, and its link to the cart is only that the dune is steep.

ideas.title: Wet sand is a road: the tide decides when to drive
ideas.critique: Moisture-dependent Bekker parameters and a tide clock are sound plumbing, but as pitched it is a hidden parameter change with nothing driving on it yet, so the most likely version is shinier sand and a moving waterline. A tide is the expected next thing for a beach.

ideas.title: The cart's first shove: friends push it off the plank end
ideas.critique: This is the road's own next step, word for word, so nobody will be surprised by it, though friends pushing with real foot traction and a cart that stops dead in sand is the part a player will actually use. Who pushes where and laying a plank in time is a real little game if the stop really comes from the bulldozing physics and not a threshold.
